subject: High request latency and 5xx spike - suspected proxy/DNS cascade
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@novaretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-09-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/504s and 200ms p90 increase

Ben —

We started seeing a pronounced increase in end-user latency and a short-lived 5xx spike across multiple services starting at ~07:45 PDT. The requests that fail are going through our proxy cluster before reaching Redwood's inference endpoints; we see a lot of retransmits and timeouts on DNS lookups for model-hosting endpoints. Attached: a small tcpdump from node-12 and aggregated app logs.

Initial symptoms:
- P90 latency climbed from 120ms to ~520ms for text-generation calls
- 502/504 rate moved from ~0.02% to 3.6% for a 17-minute window
- Errors correlate to calls routed through proxy-batch-3

We've opened INF-4627 on our side and can share temporary credentials for captures if needed. This is customer-impacting for our checkout flows. We need immediate help identifying whether this is on our peering path, a DNS TTL flapping, or something on the Redwood edge/proxy.

Attachments: tcpdump_nova_node-12.pcap (pcap), novaretail-customer-logs-09-04.log (text)

—Alex (on-call, NovaRetail Ops)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@novaretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-09-04T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/504s and 200ms p90 increase

Alex —

Thanks for the quick report and the attachments. I'm escalating this internally and will coordinate a bridge. Initial ask: can you share the hostnames you were resolving that showed intermittent NX/TIMEOUTs? Also, please confirm whether you observed any proxy config changes around 07:30–07:50.

Jordan — looping you in for network-path traces and quick hypothesis triage. Evelyn — FYI for potential exec alerting depending on impact.

I'll set up a short call in 10 mins.

—Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-09-04T08:35:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: NovaRetail latency/escalation — immediate triage

Team —

Summary: NovaRetail is reporting a customer-impacting spike in latency and 5xxs correlated with DNS timeouts and increased retransmits on traffic routed via their internal proxy cluster. They attached tcpdump and app logs (attached here). Key asks:
1) Can infra confirm whether our edge NLBs saw elevated SYN retransmits or connection timeouts for NovaRetail flows between 07:40–08:00 PDT?
2) Can we check whether the VPC peering path used by NovaRetail has any recent route flap or MTU blackhole events?
3) If not obvious from infra counters, let's run an overlay test (tracepath/mtr) from our closest POP to the hostnames in the logs and compare DNS responses.

Rishi — if you can pull dnsmasq/DNS resolver metrics and check for TTL mismatches or cache evictions around the window, that'd be helpful.

I've included the customer's JIRA and their capture. If this escalates to exec (they are pushing this up internally) we'll likely need a short executive brief.

Attachments included: nova-prod-traces_20290904.zip

—Ben
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ops Team <ops@novaretail.com>
Date: 2029-09-04T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: NovaRetail latency/escalation — immediate triage

Ben / team —

Quick update from the network side after looking at the captures and our POP telemetry:
- Edge NLBs in us-west-2 did show a burst of connections with incomplete TCP handshakes from a set of NovaRetail egress IPs between 07:42–07:58 PDT, consistent with retransmits noted in the pcap.
- Our DNS resolver logs show an abnormal number of SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN responses for the model-hosting.* domains that map to our peered subnet during the same window. TTLs were normal, but one resolver instance did restart at 07:47 for an unrelated maintenance job; it should have rejoined seamlessly, but it may have caused a cache warm-up and more upstream queries.
- Interesting correlation: NovaRetail's proxy-batch-3 is doing connection pooling and reusing transports; when DNS responses were delayed, a subset of pooled connections attempted backend reconnection and hit firewall inspection timeouts inside their proxy, manifesting as 502/504.

Action taken:
- I disabled a single resolver node from the pool and flushed DNS cache to steady-state (11:00 UTC).
- Requested packet capture from our egress to NovaRetail to validate path MTU/fragmentation — awaiting logs.

Next steps: Jordan will coordinate a joint postmortem with NovaRetail; Ben please advise if you want exec comms now.

—Jordan
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Connors <ops@novaretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-09-04T16:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/504s and 200ms p90 increase

Thanks for the investigation and the quick flush — we saw recovery begin around 11:05 UTC. We ran internal checks and confirmed there was a short configuration rollout in the proxy-batch-3 cluster at 07:40 PDT that coincided with the resolver restart you mentioned. The rollout changed connection idle timeouts which increased reuse behavior; combined with a transient DNS resolver restart this produced a cascade: delayed DNS -> stale pooled connections -> firewall inspection stalls -> 502/504.

We've attached a short summary and the NovaRetail postmortem stub (they linked INF-4627). We'll schedule a 1-hour joint postmortem tomorrow to capture timeline and action items.

Attachments: novaretail-postmortem-draft.md (text)

Appreciate the fast triage. If you think executive-level notice is helpful, flag us and we'll craft a joint note.

—Alex
NovaRetail Ops
